vocabulary.meaning_en: meeting people in your industry to share information and find business
vocabulary.example: Conferences are great for networking.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person you know who can help you in business
vocabulary.example: I made some useful contacts at the conference.

vocabulary.meaning_en: your phone number, email and address
vocabulary.example: Could I have your contact details?

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small card with your name, job and contact details
vocabulary.example: Here's my business card.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person whose job is to sell a company's products
vocabulary.example: She works as a Sales Executive.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person or company that might buy from you in the future
vocabulary.example: We met three potential customers today.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a customer who already buys from you
vocabulary.example: Tom talked to our existing customers.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to advertise something to make people buy it
vocabulary.note_en: It can also mean give someone a higher job.
vocabulary.example: We went to the fair to promote our products.

vocabulary.meaning_en: all the companies that make or sell one type of thing
vocabulary.example: She has worked in the food industry for ten years.

vocabulary.meaning_en: providing food and drinks for events or restaurants
vocabulary.example: We sell plastic fruit to the catering industry.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a small book with pictures and information about products
vocabulary.example: I'll send you one of our brochures.

vocabulary.meaning_en: in a few words, for a short time
vocabulary.example: Can I briefly tell you about our company?

vocabulary.meaning_en: to meet someone and talk about what has happened
vocabulary.example: I need to catch up with my manager.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (informal) to talk in a friendly way to important people to get business
vocabulary.example: He spent the evening schmoozing clients.

vocabulary.meaning_en: friendly and liking to talk
vocabulary.example: Be chatty and friendly at events.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person you don't know
vocabulary.example: It's hard to talk to strangers at first.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to start talking about the important work topic
vocabulary.example: OK, let's get down to business.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to give something and receive something in return
vocabulary.example: We exchanged business cards.

vocabulary.meaning_en: right or suitable for the situation
vocabulary.example: Is it appropriate to give him my card now?

vocabulary.meaning_en: an arrangement of things for people to see
vocabulary.example: The cheese display looked lovely.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the general state of the economy
vocabulary.example: It's a tough economic climate.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to reduce the number of workers
vocabulary.example: The company had to cut staff.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an event where prizes are given
vocabulary.example: The awards ceremony starts at seven.

fine_lines.title: existing customer vs potential customer
fine_lines.explanation_ar: existing customer عميل يشتري منك الآن بالفعل. potential customer عميل قد يشتري منك في المستقبل.
fine_lines.explanation_en: An existing customer already buys from you. A potential customer might buy from you in the future.

examples.sentence: Anna met a potential customer at the conference.

fine_lines.title: contact vs contact details
fine_lines.explanation_ar: contact شخص تعرفه ويمكن أن يساعدك في العمل. contact details هي المعلومات: الهاتف والبريد الإلكتروني والعنوان.
fine_lines.explanation_en: A contact is a person. Contact details are the information (phone, email, address).

examples.sentence: He is a useful contact in the food industry.
Please write your contact details on this form.

expressions.phrase: Excuse me, hello, I'm Anna. I work as a Sales Executive at Tip Top Trading.
expressions.meaning_ar: عذرًا، مرحبًا، أنا آنا. أعمل مسؤولة مبيعات في شركة تيب توب تريدينغ.
expressions.meaning_en: A polite way to introduce yourself and your job.
expressions.example: Excuse me, hello, I'm Omar. I work as an engineer at Delta Systems.

expressions.phrase: Can you tell me about your company?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل يمكنك أن تحدثني عن شركتك؟
expressions.meaning_en: Please explain what your company does.
expressions.example: Nice to meet you. Can you tell me about your company?

expressions.phrase: Can I briefly tell you about what our company does?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل يمكنني أن أحدثك باختصار عما تقوم به شركتنا؟
expressions.meaning_en: May I explain our business in a few words?
expressions.example: Can I briefly tell you about what our company does? We make office furniture.

expressions.phrase: I think we might be able to help you.
expressions.meaning_ar: أظن أننا قد نتمكن من مساعدتك.
expressions.meaning_en: Our company may have a solution for you.
expressions.example: You need cheaper printing? I think we might be able to help you.

expressions.phrase: Here's my business card should you want to call.
expressions.meaning_ar: هذه بطاقتي في حال أردت الاتصال.
expressions.meaning_en: Take my card in case you want to phone me.
expressions.example: Here's my business card should you want to call me next week.

expressions.phrase: If I could have your contact details, I'll send you one of our brochures.
expressions.meaning_ar: إذا أعطيتني بيانات التواصل، فسأرسل لك أحد كتيباتنا.
expressions.meaning_en: Give me your details and I'll send information.
expressions.example: If I could have your contact details, I'll send you our price list.

expressions.phrase: So nice to have met you.
expressions.meaning_en: A polite thing to say when you leave someone you just met.
expressions.example: Thank you for your time. So nice to have met you.

grammar.title: should you want to... (formal 'if')
grammar.explanation_ar: في الأسلوب الرسمي يمكن أن نضع should في بداية الشرط بدل if: should you want to call = if you want to call. هذا الأسلوب مهذب جدًا ومناسب للعمل.
grammar.explanation_en: In formal English, 'should you + verb' means 'if you + verb'. It sounds very polite.
examples: Here's my business card should you want to call.
Should you need any help, please let me know.
Should you have any questions, email me.

grammar.title: Can I...? / Can you...? for polite requests
grammar.explanation_ar: Can I + فعل لطلب الإذن، و Can you + فعل لطلب شيء من الآخر. ويمكن جعلها أكثر تهذيبًا باستخدام Could أو إضافة please.
grammar.explanation_en: Use 'Can I...?' to ask permission and 'Can you...?' to ask someone to do something. 'Could' is more polite.
examples: Can you tell me about your company?
Can I briefly tell you about what we do?
Could I have your contact details?

grammar.title: might for possibility
grammar.explanation_ar: might + الفعل الأساسي تعني الاحتمال، وتبدو أكثر تواضعًا وتهذيبًا من will: we might be able to help you.
grammar.explanation_en: Use might + base verb for possibility; it sounds modest and polite.
examples: I think we might be able to help you.

questions.question: What is 'networking'?
choices: meeting people in your industry to help your business
questions.explanation_ar: networking بناء علاقات مهنية لمصلحة العمل.
questions.explanation_en: It's meeting people to help your business.

questions.question: Here's my business card ___ you want to call.
questions.explanation_ar: should you want to = if you want to (أسلوب رسمي).
questions.explanation_en: 'Should you want to' is formal for 'if you want to'.

questions.question: A customer who might buy from you in the future is a ___ customer.
questions.explanation_en: Potential means possible in the future.

questions.question: Can I ___ tell you about what our company does?
What does Anna give Jane so she can call her?
'Let's get down to business' means ___.
questions.explanation_en: It means let's start on the important topic.

questions.question: Choose the most polite sentence.
choices: Could I have your contact details?

questions.question: I think we ___ be able to help you.
Which word means 'a person you don't know'?
questions.explanation_en: A stranger is someone you don't know.

questions.question: A small book with information and pictures about products is a ___.
